Requirements/Deep merge of nested configuration objects

Requirement · high criticality

Deep merge of nested configuration objects

Merge layered configuration (defaults, environment file, request overrides) without mutating the inputs. Inputs can originate from parsed JSON, so the merge must not allow an attacker to control the prototype of the returned object.

Owner: platform-securityCadence: 180 daysCreated 20 Oct 202612 candidates
Decision ApprovedActive

Adopt @fastify/deepmerge

Only candidate that satisfies every constraint: OIDC trusted publishing with SLSA provenance, zero dependencies, bundled types, active maintenance, and not affected by CVE-2026-93753. Also the fastest in the benchmark.

Build vs buy scores the capability, not this package. A rejected package can still be a capability worth buying from a maintained alternative.

Constraints

  • Zero runtime dependencies
  • CI-published with verifiable provenance
  • Bundled or resolvable TypeScript types
  • No unfixed high or critical advisories
  • Active maintenance (release within 12 months)
  • Works from both CommonJS and ESM consumers

Out of scope

  • Schema validation
  • Diffing or patching
  • YAML serialisation

Decision rationale

Adopt @fastify/deepmerge as the primary implementation: it is the only candidate that combines OIDC trusted publishing, SLSA provenance, zero runtime dependencies, bundled types, active maintenance and immunity to CVE-2026-93753. deepmerge-ts is approved as the fallback for cyclic inputs or Map/Set merging, at the cost of a long-lived NPM_TOKEN in its release pipeline. deepmerge is dropped because the vulnerability has no upstream fix and is invisible to npm audit. ts-deepmerge, merge-deep, lodash.merge, @corex/deepmerge, deep-extend and the CVE-fork packages are rejected; defu, merge-anything and @75lb/deep-merge remain on hold and are not approved for this requirement.

Review timeline

  1. 20 Oct 2026 deep-extend Avoid Unmaintained since 2018 and the subject of a critical prototype-pollution advisory. Do not use.
  2. 20 Oct 2026 deepmerge Avoid Do not use. Affected by CVE-2026-93753 (CVSS 8.7), the fix PR was closed unmerged, no release since March 2023, and npm audit does not flag it.
  3. 20 Oct 2026 @stackline/deepmerge Avoid New single-maintainer fork that markets itself on fixing CVE-2026-93753. It may well be correct, but with 246 weekly downloads, no independent review and no track record it is not a whitelisting candidate.
  4. 20 Oct 2026 lodash.merge Avoid Frozen since 2019 and carries lodash's ongoing advisory stream. Prototype pollution was fixed in 4.6.2, but there is no path to future fixes.
  5. 20 Oct 2026 merge-deep Avoid Three direct dependencies expand to 13 installed packages, no release since 2021, and no types. Avoid.
  6. 20 Oct 2026 @corex/deepmerge Avoid No repository URL published to npm and no release since 2023. Source and provenance cannot be verified. Avoid.
  7. 20 Oct 2026 ts-deepmerge Avoid Good types and a tiny footprint, but releases are not built or published by CI: the repository has no .github directory at all. Fails the release-integrity constraint.
  8. 20 Oct 2026 @75lb/deep-merge Hold Actively maintained but pulls in lodash and typical, defeating the zero-dependency constraint. ESM-only and no types. Hold.
  9. 20 Oct 2026 merge-anything Hold Reasonable API and active, but ESM-only, one dependency, 472 KB installed, no type declarations and no publish workflow. Hold unless a specific feature is needed.
  10. 20 Oct 2026 defu Hold Well-maintained and fast, but it implements defaults semantics rather than overwrite merge, and it has no publish workflow. Keep it for filling defaults only; do not adopt it for this task.
  11. 20 Oct 2026 deepmerge-ts Adopt Strong runner-up and the better choice when inputs may be cyclic or contain Map/Set. Best type inference in the field, zero deps, active, published with SLSA provenance. Falls short only on release ergonomics: it authenticates with a long-lived NPM_TOKEN rather than OIDC trusted publishing.
  12. 20 Oct 2026 @fastify/deepmerge Adopt Only candidate that satisfies every constraint: OIDC trusted publishing with SLSA provenance, zero dependencies, bundled types, active maintenance, and not affected by CVE-2026-93753. Also the fastest in the benchmark.
